## E05 historical audit

**Scope and sources.** The supplied record covers one historical run, I round 1, not a cross-batch sample. All event IDs are supplied, but individual event strings were clipped at 1,800 characters; the separately supplied initial prompt, online events, final patch and formal evaluation were not subject to that event-field clipping. References below use one-based `main_agent` event numbers in `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_08/lanes/codex_parallel_08_lane0/codex_parallel_08_lane0_I_r1/infer_logs/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/turn_1/trajs.json`.

**Task and work.** The public task required recursive `delegate_task` execution, a single JSON-string tool result returned to the parent, matching tool-use identity, and distinct unknown-agent, sub-agent-error and circular-delegation behavior. The student created a branch from `main` (events 3–4), inspected the handler, registry, providers and tests (events 5–20, 27–32), and built a mock reproduction. Its first run failed technically because top-level await was compiled as CJS; after relocation it exposed the behavioral gap: one provider call rather than at least three (events 23–26).

The nonempty final patch at `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_08/lanes/codex_parallel_08_lane0/codex_parallel_08_lane0_I_r1/infer_logs/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/turn_1/patch.diff` implements recursive execution, accumulated text, continuation, target and cycle checks, bounds, and Anthropic tool translation. It also carries tool IDs through the Claude Code provider. This is executable adoption of directions overlapping the received reference, not merely the student’s closing claim; the evidence does not isolate which ideas were caused by the teacher rather than the public task or code inspection. The patch emits a `tool_result` object in stream `data`, while serializing it for the resumed provider request; the formal failures below do not by themselves establish the precise failure mechanism. Commit `86388ec` on `fix/recursive-agent-delegation` is recorded (events 49–50).

**Teacher knowledge and independent work.** The captured prompt `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_08/lanes/codex_parallel_08_lane0/codex_parallel_08_lane0_I_r1/infer_logs/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/turn_1/system_prompt_actual.json` actually contained a reference identifying suspended-turn continuation, adapter translation, relevant files, cycle detection, cancellation, identity and suggested tests. Its instructions also demanded independent verification and prohibited revealing the reference. The student did inspect the named code and independently constructed and revised a reproduction; this is evidence of exploration, not evidence of uninfluenced work.

One online check delivered a question about capturing the resumed request and inspecting Anthropic identity and block shape, recorded in `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_08/lanes/codex_parallel_08_lane0/codex_parallel_08_lane0_I_r1/infer_logs/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/turn_1/online_teacher_events.json`. The subsequent executable reproduction asserted result content and matching IDs and inspected a mocked Anthropic request (events 45–46); this supports behavioral uptake, though not a causal estimate. Archive Hint links alone do not establish receipt, and after-round reviews were not input to this round.

**Checks and outcome.** Initial type-check and build failures were missing generated version and frontend artifacts, respectively (events 35–38). After building the frontend, builds, type-check and the narrow mock reproduction passed; the local handler suite had six passes and one abort-controller cleanup failure (events 39–40; full online event record; event 51). The later identity reproduction passed and was removed (events 45–48). These local checks are not the formal grade.

The separate formal evaluation at `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_08/lanes/codex_parallel_08_lane0/codex_parallel_08_lane0_I_r1/eval_output/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/eval_result.json` applied the 12,119-byte patch and recorded P2P 31/31, F2P 2/7, partial 0.868421052631579 and binary reward 0. Five named delegation cases failed with `expected null not to be null`. Thus this was a substantive but formally unsolved implementation, not an empty-patch or merely setup failure. The verifier’s exit code 0 indicates the evaluation ran, not task success.

**Conditions and limits.** The recorded model was `gpt-6.1-terra`, effort high, SDK entrypoint, bypass-permissions mode, Node v24.12.0, 25 main tools and one teacher check; wall time was about 623 seconds. The student ended normally with `end_turn`, not a recorded budget or technical stop. Actual CLI usage and billing are unavailable: zero-valued SDK usage/cost with unknown cost basis is not evidence of zero historical cost. Budgets and comparability to batch12/source13 are unknown. No no-Hint full pass or other historical round is supplied here, so neither teacher necessity nor a regression can be inferred. Even a finite full formal pass elsewhere would not prove the entire public contract. Broader testing of continuation and error paths is a plausible transferable hypothesis, not measured transfer or an ablation-ranked lesson.
